summary:
AEGIS (Astronaut Evaluation, Guidance, and Integrated Health System) is an offline-capable, sensor-based health monitoring and readiness support application designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions.

Integrating directly with wearable spacesuit sensors, AEGIS captures real-time physiological data—including heart rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure, and body temperature—and evaluates these metrics against safe baselines to trigger automated alerts when anomalies occur. 

To address potential health dips, the system executes an Adaptive Health Recovery process that recommends targeted response steps, tracks their completion, and reassesses vitals to dynamically update the astronaut's readiness status.

This solution is critical because deep-space missions face severe communication delays and blackouts with Earth, making real-time ground support impossible. By automating data capture and pairing continuous monitoring with guided, on-board recovery protocols, AEGIS eliminates tedious manual logging and empowers crews to make fast, informed health decisions independently.
details:
AEGIS is an offline-capable astronaut health monitoring and readiness application designed for long-duration space missions. It is designed to receive health readings from wearable spacesuit sensors, evaluate them against configured parameters, and generate alerts when unusual values are detected. It also provides predefined response activities, tracks their completion, and reassesses health readings to update readiness status.

AEGIS helps reduce manual data entry, centralize health information, and provide accessible monitoring and recovery guidance even when communication with Earth is limited. Its intended impact is to improve astronaut health awareness, support early identification of unusual readings, and promote organized onboard health management.

The application was developed using Kotlin and Java for programming, XML for the interface layout, and Android Studio as the development environment. ChatGPT and Google Gemini were also used as AI-assisted tools during development.

Its creative approach connects health monitoring, alerts, guided activities, progress tracking, and readiness reassessment into one continuous process. The team considered communication delays, limited medical assistance, physiological changes in space, offline accessibility, and the importance of distinguishing monitoring alerts from professional medical diagnosis.
